description: We are building ORBiALOG, an engineering platform that identifies micro-scale Earth analogs matching Lunar and Martian environments while calculating physics compensation factors (gravity, atmosphere, and radiation) for mission hardware testing. Led by an engineering student focused on system architecture and UI/UX, we have a clear blueprint ready. Looking for teammates skilled in Python/Data Science, GIS, Frontend (React), or Pitching!
summary:
ORBiALOG (Orbital to Terrestrial Planetary Analog Discovery Engine) is a scientific platform that discovers locations on Earth with environmental and geological conditions similar to regions on the Moon and Mars. Our team developed an automated remote-sensing pipeline and interactive 3D dashboard to help researchers identify potential planetary analog sites.

The system analyzes 10 physical and spectral dimensions using satellite observations and planetary datasets from NASA and Google Earth Engine. It applies Mahalanobis Distance with Ledoit-Wolf covariance estimation to compare planetary environments against 11,466 locations worldwide, identifying the most promising matches.

Our analysis identified two exceptional analog candidates: the Dasht-e Lut Basin in Iran, with 93.7% similarity to a Martian environment, and the Harrat Khaybar volcanic field in Saudi Arabia, with 89% similarity to lunar basalt terrain.

ORBiALOG aims to make planetary exploration research more efficient by helping scientists discover new terrestrial testing environments, improve mission preparation, and reduce the time and cost of identifying suitable analog locations.
details: ORBiALOG (Orbital to Terrestrial Planetary Analog Discovery Engine) is an intelligent scientific platform designed to discover and analyze locations on Earth that have environmental and geological characteristics similar to specific regions on the Moon and Mars. Its main purpose is to help scientists and space exploration teams identify suitable planetary analog sites on Earth, allowing them to test technologies, study geological conditions, and prepare for future space missions. The project works by collecting and analyzing satellite and planetary data from NASA and other Earth observation sources. It uses 10 physical and spectral dimensions, including surface temperature, terrain slope, roughness, albedo, precipitation, vegetation, and mineral characteristics. A statistical matching algorithm based on Mahalanobis Distance and Ledoit-Wolf covariance estimation compares planetary environments with more than 11,000 locations worldwide to identify the most similar terrestrial sites. ORBiALOG provides an interactive 3D globe dashboard where users can explore planetary targets, discover matching locations on Earth, and compare their environmental characteristics through detailed analytical results. The project uses several technologies, including Python for scientific data processing and analysis, TypeScript and Node.js for backend development, React 18 and Three.js for the interactive frontend, Express.js for REST APIs, and MongoDB Atlas for data storage. It also integrates Google Earth Engine, NASA Earthdata, and NASA's Planetary Data System to access scientific datasets. What makes ORBiALOG creative is its combination of planetary science, remote sensing, statistical intelligence, and interactive 3D visualization in one unified platform. Instead of relying only on well-known planetary analog locations, it systematically searches thousands of locations to discover potentially overlooked environments. The intended impact is to support more efficient space exploration research, reduce the time and cost of identifying terrestrial testing environments, and help scientists prepare for future Moon and Mars missions using real scientific data.
